ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r2.claim: To inherit what he says means stripping him of wealth and children so God receives them as heir; the verb says in the present while its meaning is past: what he said.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r2.anchor: ونرثه ما يقول أي نسلبه المال والولد فنكون كالوارث له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r3.speaker: الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī says God will make the Paradise the man wishes for belong to someone else.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي: نجعل ما يتمنى من الجنة لغيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r4.speaker: أبو سهيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r4.claim: Abū Suhayl says God deprives him of the wealth and children he wishes for and assigns them to another.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r4.anchor: وقال أبو سهيل: نحرمه ما يتمناه من المال والولد ونجعله لغيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī suggests the boast concerns hoped-for worldly wealth and children: even if granted, they will be taken away, and he will come alone after death, as in the verse 'You have come to Us singly.' Alternatively, death ends his boasting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r5.anchor: هب أنا أعطيناه ما اشتهاه إما نرثه منه في العاقبة ويأتينا فردا غدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r6.speaker: النحاس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r6.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says God preserves the man's words against him for the final outcome, as scholars are called heirs of the prophets because they preserve their words.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r6.anchor: ونرثه ما يقول معناه نحفظه عليه للعاقبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p295/r7.claim: Fardan conveys humiliation and lack of supporters.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The response rejects the boast furiously: disbelief brings punishment that increases for arrogance, and on Judgment Day the claimant loses all God-given possessions and appears alone and empty-handed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: On the Day of Judgement, such a person will have no helpers or their deities or intercessors to save him

BURSEVI:v5p273/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p273/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p273/r1.claim: At death God inherits what he says, meaning the wealth and children received in this world; his future boast has no object beyond them.
BURSEVI:v5p273/r1.anchor: أي : مسمى ما يقول ومصداقه وهو ما أوتيه

BURSEVI:v5p273/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p273/r2.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v5p273/r2.claim: The cited commentary says God strips away what He gave him.

BURSEVI:v5p273/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p273/r3.speaker: العيون
BURSEVI:v5p273/r3.claim: The cited source parses mā as appositional: God destroys him and transfers wealth and children to someone else.
BURSEVI:v5p273/r3.anchor: وقال في "العيون" ما بدل من هاء نرثه بدل اشتمال

BURSEVI:v5p273/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p273/r4.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p273/r4.claim: Al-Kashifi paraphrases this as inheriting the wealth and children he claimed would be given to him tomorrow.
BURSEVI:v5p273/r4.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (وميراث ميكيريم آنه ميكويدكه فردا بمن خواهند داد

BURSEVI:v5p273/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p273/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p273/r5.claim: He comes alone on the Day of Resurrection, without wealth or children from this life, much less any added share.
BURSEVI:v5p273/r5.anchor: وحيدا خاليا لا يصحبه مال ولا ولد كان له في الدنيا

BURSEVI:v5p273/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p273/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p273/r6.claim: The deluded claim fortunes and offspring in this life and salvation and rank in the next, mocking renunciants; they fail to see attachment brings distance and leaves them unsupported.
BURSEVI:v5p273/r6.anchor: أهل الغرور يدعون الإحراز للفضيلتين المال والولد في الدنيا والنجاة

BURSEVI:v5p273/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p273/r7.speaker: الكمال الخجندي
BURSEVI:v5p273/r7.claim: Al-Kamal al-Khujandi's couplet says breaking the idol of conceit in the lovers' faith is better than a hundred acts of worship.
BURSEVI:v5p273/r7.anchor:
قال الكمال الخجندي :
بشكن بت غروركه دردين عاشقان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r1.claim: God will take back at the man's death the worldly wealth and children he claimed; ما refers to their substance, and the tense recalls what he received.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r1.anchor: نسلب ذلك وناخذه بموته اخذ الوارث ما يرثه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r2.claim: ما may be an appositive explaining the pronoun or the direct object; the man comes alone at resurrection without his supposed advantage.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r2.anchor: بدل من الضمير بدل اشتمال وأمامفعول به أي نرث منه ما اتيناه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r3.claim: His reading makes the point explicit: God inherits what the man had and he arrives alone with neither money nor child.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r3.anchor: ونرثه ما عنده وياتينا فردا لا مال له ولا ولد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r4.speaker: أبو سهل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r4.claim: An alternative says God denies him the future wealth and children he claimed and gives them to other deserving people; this presumes no procreation in Paradise.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r4.anchor: المعنى نحرمه ما زعم أنه يناله في الآخرة من المال والولد ونعطيه لغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r5.speaker: مجاهد وطاوس وإبراهيم النخعي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r5.claim: They deny procreation in Paradise, citing reports that its people have no offspring and a long report from Laqit ibn ʿAmir.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r5.anchor: مجاهد وطاوس وابراهيم النخعى : بعدم التوالد احتجاجا بما في حديث لقيط

ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r6.speaker: ابن منده
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r6.claim: Ibn Mandah says only a denier or an ignorant person rejects the report of Laqit.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r6.anchor: وقال فيه أبو عبد الله بن منده لا ينكره إلا جاحد أو جاهل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r7.speaker: أبو ذر العقيلي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r7.claim: A report from the Prophet says the people of Paradise will have no child.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r7.anchor: قال : ان أهل الجنة لا يكون لهم ولد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r8.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r8.claim: A Tirmidhi report says that when a believer desires a child in Paradise, conception, birth, and growth to maturity occur in one hour; Tirmidhi calls it gharīb.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r8.anchor: وقالت فرقة بالتوالد احتجاجا بما أخرجه الترمذي في جامعه عن أبى سعيد الخدرى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r9.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r9.claim: Abu Nuʿaym transmits another report in which the Prophet confirms that Paradise's people can have a child as soon as one wishes.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r9.anchor: وبما أخرجه أبو نعيم عن أبى سعيد أيضا قيل يا رسول الله ايولد لأهل الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r10.claim: The no-procreation side answers that these reports deny only ordinary worldly reproduction; al-Bayhaqi calls the latter report weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132/r10.anchor: واجبت عما تقدم بأن المراد نفي أن يكون توالد أو ولد على الوجه المعهود في الدنيا وتعقب ذلك بأن الحديث الأخير ضعيف كما قال البيهقي

ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r1.speaker: السفاريني
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r1.claim: Al-Safarini calls the Tirmidhi chain the best of the procreation reports but notes Tirmidhi's gharīb grading and inconsistent wordings.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r1.anchor: اجود اسانيده اسناد الترمذى وقد حمك عليه بالغرابة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r2.claim: Even if the preceding chain is hasan, its conditional wording need not mean the condition will occur; the attempted reconciliation of contrary reports is weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r2.anchor: أن فيه تعليقا بالشرط وجاز أن لا يقع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r3.speaker: السفاريني
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r3.claim: Most scholars favor no procreation, which al-Safarini supports with ten arguments, though the author says many can be debated.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r3.anchor: وبالجملة المرجح عند الأكثرين عدم التوالد ورجح ذلك السفاريني بعشرة اوجه لكن للبحث في اكثرها مجال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r4.claim: One interpretation takes ما يقول as the man's literal boast: while alive he keeps mocking, but death prevents further mockery when reality is revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : المراد بما يقول نفس القول المذكور لا مسمى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r5.claim: The objection says this assumes genuine belief in resurrection, impossible for an unbeliever; the response allows continued mockery until death exposes him.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r5.anchor: وتعقب بأن هذا مبنى على صدور القول المذكور عنه بطريق الأعتقاد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r6.claim: Another view says God preserves the boast to reproach him at judgment, where he arrives poor and without the wealth he sought; preservation is already stated by سنكتب.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r6.anchor: المعنى نحفظ قوله لنضرب به وجهه في الموقف ونعيره به

ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari imagines that God grants the requested wealth and children in life, then inherits them at judgment; al-Alusi finds this very remote, especially given the occasion report.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r7.anchor: وفي الكشاف يحتمل أنه قد تمنى وكمع أن يؤتيه الله تعالى مالا وولدا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r8.claim: فردا is circumstantial in all interpretations; it is future-oriented when wealth and children are transferred, but simple arrival alone suffices for the other views.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p132#2/r8.anchor: حال على جميع الأقوال لكن قيل : أنه حال مقدرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254#2/r3.claim: God inherits the wealth and children the man claimed by destroying him and nullifying his dominion; the inheritance concerns possessions beneath his claim to have them in the next life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254#2/r3.anchor: ونرثه ما يقول} أي ما عنده من المال والولد بإهلاكنا إياه وإبطال ملكه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254#2/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation says God preserves what the man says so He can requite him for it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: معنى قوله: {ونرثه ما يقول} أي: نحفظ ما يقول حتى نجازيه به.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254#3/r1.claim: He comes to God on Resurrection Day alone, without wealth or children.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254#3/r1.anchor: ويأتينا فردا} يوم القيامة بلا مال ولا ولد.

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:79-80/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:79-80/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:79-80/r2.claim: God inherits his wealth and children at death; he comes alone without them, or alone after abandoning his claim.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:79-80/r2.anchor: { فردا } لا يصحبه مال ولا ولد

BIQAI-FULL:v4p555/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p555/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p555/r1.claim: At death God inherits all the wealth and children the man claimed; he arrives alone after resurrection, powerless and stripped of honor and strength.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p555/r1.anchor: مسكينا منعزلا عن كل شيء لا قدرة له على مال ولا ولد

BIQAI-FULL:v4p555/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p555/r2.speaker: خباب
BIQAI-FULL:v4p555/r2.claim: Al-Bukhārī reports that Khabbāb, a smith, sought payment for a sword from al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, who demanded that he disbelieve in Muhammad; al-ʿĀṣ then claimed he would be resurrected wealthy with children and repay him, and the verse was revealed.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p555/r2.anchor: قال : كنت قينا بمكة فعملت للعاص بن وائل السهمي سيفا

DURR-FULL:v5p535/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p535/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p535/r6.claim: He says what God will inherit from the claimant is his wealth and children.
DURR-FULL:v5p535/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ونرثه ما يقول} قال: ماله وولده

DURR-FULL:v5p535/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p535/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p535/r7.claim: He also says the wealth and children are what will be inherited, and identifies the claimant as al-As ibn Wa'il.
DURR-FULL:v5p535/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ونرثه ما يقول} قال: ماله وولده

DURR-FULL:v5p535/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p535/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p535/r8.claim: He glosses what God inherits as all that the claimant possesses; Ibn Masud's reading says God inherits his possessions and he comes alone.
DURR-FULL:v5p535/r8.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ونرثه ما يقول} قال: ما عنده

QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r13.claim: God will take over what the man boasts of, leaving him separated from his children, household, servants, and people.
QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r13.anchor: لن نمتعه بأولاده وحشمه وخدمه وقومه ، ويعود إلينا منفردا عنهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p162/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p162/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p162/r3.claim: “What he says” abbreviates his lengthy blasphemy and mockery, as well as his boast of future wealth and children; 3:183 uses the same concise reference to their words.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p162/r3.anchor: و { ما يقول } في الموضعين إيجاز ، لأنه لو حكي كلامه لطال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p162/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p162/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p162/r4.claim: “We shall inherit” means God will take his actual property and children, not inherit his words; the phrase is an appositional clarification of the object pronoun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p162/r4.anchor: أي نرث أعيان ما ذكر أسماءه ، إذ لا يعقل أن يورث عنه قوله وكلامه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p162/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p162/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p162/r5.claim: Inheritance figuratively means dispossession or implies his death; it reminds him that death is near and threatens his destruction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p162/r5.anchor: والإرث : مستعمل مجازا في السلب والأخذ ، أو كناية عن لازمه وهو الهلاك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p162/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p162/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p162/r6.claim: His sons ʿAmr, a Companion, and Hishām, martyred at Ajnādayn, became Muslims; this promises the Prophet good news and gives al-ʿĀṣ grief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p162/r6.anchor: فإن العاصي ولد عمرا الصحابي الجليل وهشاما الصحابي الشهيد يوم أجنادين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r11.claim: God inherits what the unbeliever thought he would receive; his worldly property is destroyed and left behind. Inheritance is metaphorical, or his disappointment is like inheriting a failed hope.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r11.anchor: فالوراثة مستعارة ويحتمل أن يكون خيبته في الآخرة كوراثة ما أمل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r12.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's reading says “We inherit what he has.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r12.anchor: وفي حرف ابن مسعود «ونرثه ما عنده»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r13.speaker: النحاس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r13.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says God preserves the man's statement to punish him, as scholars preserve prophetic words.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r13.anchor: وقال النحاس نرثه ما يقول معناه نحفظه عليه لنعاقبه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r14.claim: Fardan conveys humiliation and lack of support.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r14.anchor: وقوله فردا يتضمن ذلته وقلة انتصاره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261#3/r1.claim: One view says God takes the wealth and children the man claimed would be his in Paradise and gives them to other Muslims; al-Farraʾ selects this view.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261#3/r1.anchor: نرثه ما يقول انه له في الجنة فنجعله لغيره من المسلمين قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس واختاره الفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261#3/r2.claim: Another view says God inherits the man's worldly wealth and children by destroying him and ending his ownership; al-Zajjaj paraphrases this as stripping him and transferring them to others.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261#3/r2.anchor: نرث ما عنده من المال والولد باهلاكنا إياه وإبطال ملكه وهو مروي عن ابن عباس ايضا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261#3/r3.claim: He comes to God alone, without wealth or children.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r1.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r1.claim: Khabbab says al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il refused to pay his debt unless he disavowed Muhammad; when Khabbab refused, al-ʿAs claimed he would have wealth and children after resurrection, prompting revelation. The canonical collections transmit it through several routes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r1.anchor: عن خباب بن الأرت قال: كنت رجلا قينا، وكان لي على العاص بن وائل دين، فأتيته أتقاضاه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r3.claim: Al-ʿAwfi transmits Ibn ʿAbbas's account that companions sought debts from al-ʿAs, who argued that since they expected heavenly wealth and scripture, he too would receive wealth, children, and a book like theirs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r3.anchor: وقال العوفي عن ابن عباس: إن رجالا من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كانوا يطلبون العاص بن وائل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p261/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p261/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p261/r2.claim: God takes away the wealth and children the man claimed he would receive, so he comes alone, stripped of them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p261/r2.anchor: نسلبه منه، عكس ما قال: إنه يؤتى في الدار الآخرة مالا وولدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p261/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p261/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p261/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies what God inherits as the man's property and children, namely al-ʿAs's boast.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p261/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {ونرثه ما يقول} : ماله وولده، وذلك الذي قال العاص بن وائل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p261/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p261/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p261/r4.claim: Qatada says God inherits what the man possessed and claimed; Ibn Masʿud's reading says “what he has.” Qatada also says he arrives with no wealth or children.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p261/r4.anchor: عن قتادة: {ونرثه ما يقول} قال: ما عنده، وهو قوله: {لأوتين مالا وولدا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p261/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p261/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p261/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says God inherits everything accumulated and done in worldly life, and the man arrives alone without any of it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p261/r5.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: {ونرثه ما يقول} قال: ما جمع من الدنيا، وما عمل فيها

JISHUMI:v6p4610/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4610/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4610/r4.claim: The one who deserves punishment will have no helper or useful thing when he comes to God alone.
JISHUMI:v6p4610/r4.anchor: ويأتينا فردا بأن من يستحق العذاب لا ناصر له ولا شيء ينفعه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r5.claim: “We inherit what he says” can mean stripping away the wealth and children he claims he will receive and giving them to someone deserving.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r5.anchor: نزوي عنه ما زعم أنه يناله في الآخرة ونعطيه من يستحقه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r6.claim: Alternatively, what he says names his hoped-for wealth and children; even if granted in this life, they are ultimately taken from him and he comes alone.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أنه قد تمنى وطمع أن يؤتيه الله في الدنيا مالا وولدا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r7.claim: Or he says this only while alive; death silences him, or God preserves the words in his record to expose and shame him at the gathering.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r7.anchor: ما دام حيا ، فإذا قبضناه حلنا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r8.claim: He comes poor and alone, deprived of wealth, children, and his wish, bearing both the consequences of his boast and the loss of what he coveted.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r8.anchor: من المال والولد ، لم نوله سؤله ولم نؤته متمناه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r9.claim: On the first interpretation, “alone” describes a state everyone shares on arrival before their later outcomes diverge.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p41/r9.anchor: حال مقدرة نحو { فادخلوها خالدين } لأنه وغيره سواء

FARRA:v2p170/r13.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p170/r13.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p170/r13.claim: God will inherit what al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil claimed to own in Paradise, assigning it to another; the sinner arrives without wealth or children.
FARRA:v2p170/r13.anchor: بن وائل أنه له في الجنة فتجعله لغيره

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r9.claim: God's inheriting his boast may mean stripping him of worldly wealth and children or depriving him of the wealth and children imagined for the afterlife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r9.anchor: أن الله يسلبه ما أعطاه في الدنيا من مال وولد . الثاني

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r10.claim: Coming to God alone means without wealth and children or without a protector and helper.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r10.anchor: بلا مال ولا ولد . الثاني : بلا ولي ولا ناصر

MUJAHID:v1p390#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p390#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p390#3/r1.claim: Mujahid says what God inherits from the boastful man is his wealth and children, identifying him as al-As ibn Wa'il.
MUJAHID:v1p390#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ ونرثه ما يقول ﴾ يعني ماله وولده وهو العاص بن وائل

MUQATIL:19:79-82/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:79-82/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:79-82/r4.claim: God inherits from al-ʿĀṣ the reward he claimed and gives it to someone else.

MUQATIL:19:79-82/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:79-82/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:79-82/r5.claim: Al-ʿĀṣ will come to God in the afterlife alone, with nothing from his worldly life.
MUQATIL:19:79-82/r5.anchor: العاص في الآخرة، ليس معه شىء من دنياه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#5/r1.claim: God will take away what the man claimed he would attain in the afterlife, namely wealth and children.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#5/r1.anchor: أي نزوى عنه ما زعم أنه يناله في الآخرة والمعنى مسمى ما يقول

NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#5/r2.claim: He will come alone, without wealth, children, helper, or supporter, as in the cited verse.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#5/r2.anchor: حال أي بلا مال ولا ولد كقوله ولقد جئتمونا فرادى فما يجدي عليه تمنيه وتأليه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p275#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p275#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p275#5/r1.claim: What the boastful person says God will give him means wealth and children; he will come to God alone with nothing.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p275#5/r1.anchor: {ونرثه ما يقول} أي المال والولد الذي قال: لأوتينه. {ويأتينا فردا} لا شيء معه

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r1.speaker: خباب
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r1.claim: Khabbāb had a debt owed by al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil; when pressed to deny Muḥammad, he refused until the debtor died and was raised, and al-ʿĀṣ mocked that he would repay when restored to wealth and children. The report is transmitted by Muslim and Bukhārī.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r1.anchor: عن خباب قال كان لي على العاص بن وائل دين فأتيته أتقاضاه

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r2.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say blacksmith Khabbāb had made jewelry for al-ʿĀṣ; al-ʿĀṣ mocked repayment in Paradise, claiming he would have wealth there and Khabbāb no greater entitlement.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي ومقاتل: كان خباب قينا فصاغ للعاص حليا

QURTUBI-FULL:19:79-80/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:79-80/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:79-80/r7.claim: “We inherit what he says” can mean stripping him of worldly wealth and children; Ibn ʿAbbās and others say God inherits them after destroying him.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:79-80/r7.anchor: أي نسلبه ما أعطيناه في الدنيا من مال وولد

QURTUBI-FULL:19:79-80/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:79-80/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:79-80/r8.claim: Another view is that he is denied the afterlife wealth and children he desired, which are given instead to other Muslims.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:79-80/r8.anchor: وقيل: نحرمه ما تمناه في الآخرة من مال وولد

QURTUBI-FULL:19:79-80/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:79-80/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:79-80/r9.claim: He comes alone, without wealth, children, or clan to defend him.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:79-80/r9.anchor: أي منفردا لا مال له ولا ولد ولا عشيرة تنصره

RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r15.claim: God inherits away the wealth and children the man claimed, and the man comes alone in the afterlife, like all people return individually as first created.
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r15.anchor: أي يزول عنه ما وعده من مال وولد فلا يعود كما لا يعود الإرث إلى من خلفه

STUDYQURAN:19:79/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:79/r3.speaker: Ṭ, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:19:79/r3.claim: God inherits the wealth and children the disbeliever claims he will possess, since God is the Inheritor and all things return to Him.
STUDYQURAN:19:79/r3.anchor: God shall inherit from him that which he claims; that is, God will “inherit” his wealth and his children (Ṭ, Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:19:79/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:79/r4.speaker: Ṭ, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:19:79/r4.claim: Coming to God alone means arriving without the wealth and children that brought honor and security in worldly life.
STUDYQURAN:19:79/r4.anchor: devoid of the wealth and children that were a source of honor and security for him in this world (Ṭ, Ṭs)

TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r1.speaker: خباب
TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r1.claim: Khabbāb says al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil owed him money and refused to pay unless he renounced Muhammad; al-ʿĀṣ boasted that after resurrection he would have wealth and children, prompting these verses.
TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r1.anchor: عن خباب، قال: كنت رجلا قينا، وكان لي على العاص بن وائل دين، فأتيته أتقاضاه، فقال: والله لا أقضيك

TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that when companions collected a debt, al-ʿĀṣ mocked their promise of Paradise and boasted he would have wealth, children, and a book like theirs in the afterlife.
TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r2.anchor: فقال: ألستم تزعمون أن في الجنة فضة وذهبا وحريرا، ومن كل الثمرات؟ قالوا: بلى، قال: فإن موعدكم الآخرة،

TAB-FULL:v15p621#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p621#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p621#2/r1.claim: The man did not know the unseen or make a covenant through faith and obedience; he instead disbelieved, so God will record his boast and increase his punishment for the lie in addition to disbelief.
TAB-FULL:v15p621#2/r1.anchor: بل كذب وكفر. ثم قال تعالى ذكره: {سنكتب ما يقول} [مريم: 79] أي سنكتب ما يقول هذا الكافر بربه

TAB-FULL:v15p623/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p623/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p623/r1.claim: God will take the wealth and children the boaster claimed for the afterlife, and he will come alone without either.
TAB-FULL:v15p623/r1.anchor: حدثني علي، قال: ثنا عبد الله، قال: ثني معاوية، عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ونرثه ما يقول} [مريم: 80] نرثه

TAB-FULL:v15p623/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p623/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p623/r2.claim: Mujāhid says what God inherits is al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil's wealth and children.
TAB-FULL:v15p623/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {ونرثه ما يقول} [مريم: 80] ماله وولده، وذلك الذي قال العاصي بن وائل

TAB-FULL:v15p623/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p623/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p623/r3.claim: Qatāda interprets the inherited thing as all the man's possessions, namely his claim to receive wealth and children.
TAB-FULL:v15p623/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {ونرثه ما يقول} [مريم: 80] قال: ما عنده، وهو قوله {لأوتين مالا وولدا} [مريم: 77]

TAB-FULL:v15p623/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p623/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p623/r4.claim: The variant reading attributed to Ibn Masʿūd says God inherits what the man has.
TAB-FULL:v15p623/r4.anchor: وفي حرف ابن مسعود: ونرثه ما عنده

TAB-FULL:v15p623/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p623/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p623/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says God inherits everything the man amassed and did in worldly life; he arrives alone with nothing, small or great.
TAB-FULL:v15p623/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ونرثه ما يقول} [مريم: 80] قال: ما جمع من الدنيا وما عمل فيها.

TAB-FULL:v15p623/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p623/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p623/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the statement as God inheriting the man.
TAB-FULL:v15p623/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ونرثه ما يقول} [مريم: 80] نرثه

TABATABAI:19:80/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:80/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:80/r1.claim: On the author’s preferred reading, the man dies and leaves behind his claim that disbelief would give him wealth and children; it remains attached to him as a sin preserved by God.
TABATABAI:19:80/r1.anchor: أنه سيموت ويفنى ويترك قوله لأوتين بكفري مالا وولدا، وقد كان خطيئة لازمة له لزوم المال للإنسان محفوظة عند الله

TABATABAI:19:80/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:80/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:80/r2.claim: He comes to God alone, without anything he relied on or used for support, carrying only the statement preserved against him and facing its consequence.
TABATABAI:19:80/r2.anchor: أي وحده وليس معه شيء مما كان ينتصر به ويركن إليه بحسب وهمه

TABATABAI:19:80/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:80/r4.speaker: الأكثر
TABATABAI:19:80/r4.claim: On the majority reading, the speaker is ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil or al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who swears he will receive wealth and children in Paradise after resurrection; God asks whether he knows the unseen or has a covenant, then strips him of possessions and brings him alone.
TABATABAI:19:80/r4.anchor: بناء على كونه ناظرا إلى الإيتاء في الآخرة كما اختاره الأكثر فمعنى الآيات كما فسروها تعجب من الذي كفر بآياتنا وهو عاص بن وائل أو وليد بن المغيرة

TABATABAI:19:80#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r1.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r1.claim: The report continues that ʿĀṣ said he would return after death with wealth and children to repay Khabbāb; the author notes similar accounts from al-Ṭabarānī, Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr via al-Ḥasan and an unnamed Companion, and Ibn ʿAbbās via Companions, without grading them.
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r1.anchor: قال فإني إذا مت ثم بعثت جئتني ولي ثم مال وولد فاعطيك

TABATABAI:19:80#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r2.claim: The reports do not fit the context: they make the saying a mockery by someone who denied resurrection, whereas the passage answers it with a serious argument.
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r2.anchor: على صراحتها في كونها كلمة استهزاء لا تنطبق على الآية

TABRISI:19:78-82/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78-82/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:19:78-82/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and Ibn Zayd say God will inherit the man’s wealth and children by destroying him and nullifying his ownership.
TABRISI:19:78-82/r13.anchor: ما عنده من المال والولد بإهلاكنا إياه وإبطال ملكه عن ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد

TABRISI:19:78-82/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78-82/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:78-82/r14.claim: He will come to the Hereafter alone, without wealth, children, support, or numbers.
TABRISI:19:78-82/r14.anchor: يأتي الآخرة وحيدا بلا مال ولا ولد ولا عدة ولا عدد

THALABI:v6p229/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p229/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p229/r9.claim: The man will come to God alone in the afterlife without any worldly possessions.
THALABI:v6p229/r9.anchor: ويأتينا فردا في الآخرة ليس معه شيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p317/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p317/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p317/r1.claim: God will inherit the man’s worldly wealth and children by destroying him and ending his ownership; Ibn Masʿud’s reading says what he possesses, and the next phrase says he comes alone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p317/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {ونرثه ما يقول} فيه قولان أحدهما: (نرثه ما عنده من المال والولد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p317/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p317/r2.speaker: السدي والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p317/r2.claim: Alternatively, God inherits the Paradise property he claimed, including gold, silver, and silk, and gives it to other Muslims.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p317/r2.anchor: القول الثاني: ما قاله السدي قال: (نرثه أهله وماله الذي في الجنة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p317/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p317/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p317/r3.claim: On this reading, he will not receive the promised things and will be stripped of what he had in this world, arriving without wealth or children.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p317/r3.anchor: وعلى هذا معنى الآية: لا نعطيه ما يقول ونسلبه الذي آتيناه في الدنيا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:79-81/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:79-81/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:79-81/r2.claim: The Paradise gold and silver he claimed will be inherited for other Muslims; he will come alone without wealth, children, or servants.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:79-81/r2.anchor: ونرثه ما يقول } من أن في الجنة ذهبا وفضة، فنجعله لغيره من المسلمين { ويأتينا فردا } خاليا من ماله وولده وخدمه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r6.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r6.claim: Khabbāb reports that al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil withheld his wages unless he disavowed Muhammad, then promised to repay after resurrection from future wealth and children; Khabbāb told the Prophet, and these verses were revealed.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r6.anchor: عن خباب بن الأرت قال: كنت قينا في الجاهلية فعملت للعاصي بن وائل حتى اجتمعت لي عنده دراهم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r7.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r7.claim: Qatāda says God will inherit what the claimant possesses.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r7.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: نرثه ما عنده

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r8.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r8.claim: Mujāhid explains what is inherited as the man's wealth and children.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {ونرثه ما يقول} [مريم: 80] ماله وولده.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r9.claim: The wealth-and-children interpretation applies likewise to al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r9.anchor: وكذلك الذي قال العاصي بن وائل

SAMIN-DURR:19:82#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:82#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:82#2/r5.claim: In ونرثه ما يقول, ما may be the direct object, with the pronoun implying من; or it may be an appositive of inclusion to that pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:19:82#2/r5.anchor: يجوز في " ما " وجهان؛ أحدهما: أن تكون مفعولا بها.

SAMIN-DURR:19:82#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:82#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:82#2/r6.claim: Some supply a noun before the relative, meaning the sense or named referent of his words, since the words themselves are not inherited.
SAMIN-DURR:19:82#2/r6.anchor: وقدر بعضهم مضافا قبل الموصول، أي: نرثه معنى ما يقول،

ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r10.claim: God will take away the man's wealth and children, assign them to another, and bring him alone.
ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r10.anchor: أي نجعل المال والولد لغيره ونسلبه ذلك ويأتينا فردا

ASAD-NOTES:19:78#n68/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:78#n68/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:78#n68/r1.claim: God inheriting what the man claimed is a metaphor for taking over what once belonged to or was vested in him.
ASAD-NOTES:19:78#n68/r1.anchor: a metaphor based on the concept of one person's taking over what once belonged to, or was vested in, another

ASAD-NOTES:19:78#n69/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:78#n69/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:78#n69/r1.claim: Appearing alone means having no external support and relying only on God's grace and mercy.
ASAD-NOTES:19:78#n69/r1.anchor: bereft of any extraneous support, and thus depending on God's grace and mercy alone

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p12/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p12/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p12/r1.claim: Qatada says God will inherit what the boastful man possesses, the wealth and children he claimed he would receive.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p12/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ونرثه ما يقول ﴾ قال ما عنده وهو قوله ﴿ لأوتين مالا وولدا ﴾

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p12/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p12/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p12/r2.claim: Ibn Masud's variant reading says God will inherit what the man has.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p12/r2.anchor: وفي حرف ابن مسعود ونرثه ما عنده

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p13#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p13#4/r1.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p13#4/r1.claim: Khabbab recounts that al-As ibn Wa'il withheld wages until he renounced Muhammad and boasted of future wealth; after Khabbab told the Prophet, the passage was revealed.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p13#4/r1.anchor: عن أبي الضحى عن مسروق قال قال خباب بن الأرت كنت قينا وكنت أعمل للعاص بن وائل فاجتمع لي عليه دراهم

BUKHARI:4735/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4735/r1.speaker: خباب
BUKHARI:4735/r1.claim: Khabbab reports that al-As ibn Wa'il promised to pay his debt from wealth and children after resurrection; the passage was revealed to reject that boast and foretell punishment and his solitary return to God.
BUKHARI:4735/r1.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي الضُّحَى، عَنْ مَسْرُوقٍ، عَنْ خَبَّابٍ، قَالَ كُنْتُ رَجُلًا قَيِّنًا، وَكَانَ لِي عَلَى الْعَاصِي بْنِ وَائِلٍ دَيْنٌ
